input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: Section 12.3 expressly disclaims any exclusivity commitment by Customer, but the second Section 12.4 (p0046) prohibits Customer from acquiring any product or service that competes with Vendor for the entire term plus twenty-four months, in any territory. That acquisition bar functions as a sole-supplier obligation: it prevents us from procuring competing services from third parties, with no product-category limit, no 12-month cap, and no automatic exit for Vendor's service-level or delivery failures, so it fails the fallback and sits in walk-away territory (exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance-based exit). We therefore delete only the "acquire" prong, which restores the preferred position and removes the conflict with Section 12.3, while leaving the remaining restrictive-covenant wording untouched. Section 7.2's disclose-and-match obligation is a most-favoured-offer/right-to-match mechanic rather than exclusivity (it does not prohibit engaging another provider once honoured) and is assessed under MFN, not flagged again here.

proposal.summary: Remove the prohibition on Customer acquiring competing products or services, which operates as a de facto sole-supplier obligation.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 12.4 bars us from acquiring any competing product or service for the term plus twenty-four months, which is a de facto sole-supplier obligation and contradicts Section 12.3. We have deleted the "acquire" prong so we retain the freedom to buy from other suppliers; our position is no exclusivity commitment on Customer.

mappings.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
